T-2376: the Green Tree shoulder light gets its pointed gable cap (#1684)

* T-2376: the Green Tree shoulder light gets its pointed gable cap

One bounded, data-only trial inside the open original picture case.
`phases.frame_1833.form.enclosed_left_annex.value.shoulder.front_gable_peak_m`
goes 4.50 -> 4.85 m, so the small front-gable light over the enclosed shoulder
reads as the sharply pointed cap Andreas's detailed retrospective engraving
draws, instead of the blunt, nearly flat one the earlier value produced.
Against the builder's unchanged 4.20 m dormer head and 0.625 m roof half-span
that is about 25.6 deg -> about 46.1 deg. 4.85 m is a RECONSTRUCTED working
control chosen for the drawn shape: the plate carries no scale, dimension,
geographic camera or date, so nothing here is measured and nothing is dated.

Built on the pinned Blender, not hand-edited. Exactly one master was stale and
exactly one was rebuilt: inputs 80d47de6a302 -> bb16568756e3, MASTER 0b53a6fe ->
f213818f (269,880 -> 270,816 bytes), WEB 0154cfad -> 65863b3c (48,648 -> 48,772
bytes), derived in the same run. Every foreign registry row and producer family
is untouched.

Exported-mesh comparison of the two masters confines the change to the dormer
roof and its gable-course infill: 3,318 -> 3,330 triangles, the two dormer ridge
vertices raised 0.35 m, 24 cladding vertices added in the 4.307-4.581 m band,
every other primitive byte-identical, and the full model bounding box exactly
equal. The peak stays below the unchanged 5.0 m main-block wall head.

Controlled before/after through tools/photo_match.mjs at the unchanged camera
9439f5f7 and picture bfaa184f, only the master rebuilt. The previous
side-by-side is preserved in docs/RESEARCH/green-tree-annex-T-2376/. No sky
seam, hole or roof penetration. The closed shoulder, its lower sash and upper
light and the two separate uncovered farm wagons are retained; no shed, posts or
covered wagon returns.

The canonical review stays `differs`. Only the sharper dormer cap is marked
fixed; the shoulder's own roof slope and the left group's relative proportions
stay OPEN, Trowbridge/Gale's 1902 open wagon bay remains explicit
counterevidence with no known conversion date, and the drawing-to-drawing
upper/attic count and camera residuals stay within tolerance (T-3153). The
original ticket's wider coverage is still incomplete; T-2376 stays open/partial.

* T-2376: repair the source-use backlinks and narrow the byte-identity claim

Two bounded repairs on the integrated tree, no geometry and no new research.

The hosted gate's single red on the previous head — "Source-use backlinks match
authored claims (T-1248)", 1 of 1,140 steps — was the generated backlink index
left behind by this branch's new liberty: `tools/compile_source_use.py` re-run
through its owner takes the liberties row from 991 to 992 and
`--check` passes. 559 sources, every id resolving.

The proof prose said "every other primitive byte-identical", which is too broad.
Re-audited accessor by accessor across both masters: the master holds ten
primitives; `wall` changed (positions, normals, indices, `_CONFIDENCE`; 1,926 ->
1,950 vertices, 960 -> 972 triangles, the new vertices in the 4.307-4.850 m band)
and `roof_shingle` changed (positions and normals only — the four vertex entries
carrying the two ridge corners move in y alone, 4.500 -> 4.850, x and z
bit-identical). The other eight are byte-identical in geometry, normals, vertex
colours, `_CONFIDENCE`, indices and material, BUT `TEXCOORD_0` was repacked across
all ten, so those eight are not byte-identical as whole primitives. Those UVs are
unused: both masters declare zero textures, zero images and no material texture
reference. Corrected in the owning match record, the research dossier and STATUS,
each as a dated correction that leaves the earlier WIP wording standing where it
was first written. The accepted cap and the view's `differs` verdict are unchanged.

No producer, parameter-validator, schema or recipe-scheme edited; no mesh rebuilt
(`validate.py --stale`: 1,034 assets match their inputs, 0 stale).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-2376: file this head's two smoke readings in the standing record

mobile stage 3-4 PASS (139 passed, 0 failed, 7 m 24 s) and desktop stage 3 PASS
(107 passed, 0 failed, 7 m 09 s), both --published, both on the integrated tree
sha256:da70d3c089d1ecc4. Part 3 is the leg that covers this diff — the record's
own account on the card, and the liberties compiled into the scene. Parts 1-15
are named by `smoke_budget.mjs --for-diff` only because a changed mesh is drawn
by every part; part 14's own leg is priced at 11 m 22 s mobile and 9 m 55 s
desktop against a 10 m foreground ceiling, so it is not run here and is not
claimed.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-2376: file this head's two smoke readings in the standing record

mobile stage 3-4 (139 passed, 0 failed, 7 m 07 s) and desktop stage 3 (107
passed, 0 failed, 7 m 09 s), both SMOKE PASS on the published mirror of this
head, filed on treeHash sha256:a805c1fd4db717c4.

Filing them runs the ledger's own `prune(cap = 60)`, which keeps the newest and
the newest PASSING reading for every (viewport, part) and trims the remaining
history newest-first. Six older rows fell out that way — four of them dev's,
which the smokestate union driver had just brought in. That is the tool's
documented policy, not a hand-drop: no reading was removed by this run, and the
invariant `ask` reads is intact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

@@ -23,3 +23,62 @@ The read-only yard audit found no Green Tree-specific clearance finding with the
 This is useful partial progress on original T-2376. The genuine new-model Andreas comparison was rendered through the native owner and directly reviewed against the unchanged source camera and previous model: the low connector and turned range are visibly present. Its verdict stays `differs`, with one compound OPEN entry for the remaining closed-shoulder and range-opening disagreements. The asset-only comparison omits native yard geometry, signs and ground; published app review and the original full picture-match signoff stay open. No new photo follow-up or complete-match claim is made.
 
 The new annex geometry cites only the three held historical picture records. Chicagology's modern page remains text-only context for later historical testimony and counterevidence; its unresolved webpage rights are unchanged. The two existing static farm-wagon stands stay on their earlier reconstructed parking-apron datum after retiring the ell. Their protected historical notes describe the older ell-based derivation; L-green-tree-enclosed-left-reading-2376 amends that reasoning without moving the wagons or rebuilding the wing.
+
+## The shoulder light's gable cap — 2026-11-04 (T-2376, partial)
+
+The closed shoulder landed with a front-gable light whose cap was nearly flat: the
+builder sets the dormer wall head from the light itself (3.35 m sill + 0.70 m height
++ 0.15 m head margin = 4.20 m) over a roof half-span of (0.65 m light + 0.50 m cheeks
++ 0.10 m overhang) / 2 = 0.625 m, and a 4.50 m peak over that is a cap of about 25.6
+degrees. Andreas's detailed retrospective engraving draws a small, sharply pointed
+light there. Raising `front_gable_peak_m` to 4.85 m gives about 46.1 degrees and the
+pointed shape; the clapboard courses step up the little gable face with it.
+
+The 4.85 m is a reconstructed control for the drawn shape, not a measurement; the
+plate carries no scale, dimension, camera or date. See
+`docs/LIBERTIES.md` § L-green-tree-shoulder-dormer-cap-2376.
+
+The comparison was controlled: the same camera (`9439f5f7…`) and the same picture
+(`bfaa184f…`), only the master rebuilt. The previous side-by-side is preserved here
+as `andreas_1838-side-by-side-before-dormer-cap-20261104.jpg`; the current one is at
+`docs/RESEARCH/photo-match/green_tree_tavern/andreas_1838-side-by-side.jpg`.
+
+Independent exported-mesh comparison of the two masters confines the change to the
+dormer roof and its gable-course infill: 3,318 → 3,330 triangles; the two dormer
+ridge vertices raised 0.35 m (the four `roof_shingle` vertex entries that carry them
+move in y alone, 4.500 → 4.850, with x and z bit-identical); 24 cladding vertices
+added to the `wall` primitive in the 4.307–4.850 m band; and the full model bounding
+box exactly equal (`[-0.25, 0.0, -15.131628] … [18.177464, 8.722019, 0.355]`).
+
+**Correction, 2026-11-04 (what the other primitives actually share).** The first
+account of this trial said “every other primitive byte-identical”. That phrase was
+too broad and is withdrawn. Re-audited accessor by accessor across both masters, the
+master holds **ten** primitives, and the honest statement is narrower:
+
+- **two** primitives changed — `wall` (positions, normals, indices and
+  `_CONFIDENCE`; 1,926 → 1,950 vertices, 960 → 972 triangles) and `roof_shingle`
+  (positions and normals only, same 32 vertices and 16 triangles);
+- the **other eight** — `glass`, `brick`, `trim`, `door`, `door_panel`, `iron`,
+  `board_door`, `board_door_panel` — are byte-identical in **geometry, normals,
+  vertex colours, `_CONFIDENCE`, indices and material**;
+- **but `TEXCOORD_0` was repacked across all ten**, the eight unchanged ones
+  included, so those eight are not byte-identical as whole primitives.
+
+Those UVs are **unused**: both masters declare zero textures, zero images and no
+material texture reference, so nothing samples `TEXCOORD_0` and the repack changes
+no rendered pixel. The earlier wording is left in place as dated historical WIP where
+it was first written; this entry is the owning record. The accepted cap and the
+view's remaining `differs` verdict are unaffected. No sky seam, hole or
+roof penetration appears in the render. The closed shoulder, its lower sash and
+upper light, and the two separate uncovered farm wagons are retained; no shed, posts
+or covered wagon returns.
+
